newsitem.title: USA: U.S. disappointed Honduras won't extradite Haitian.
newsitem.headline: U.S. disappointed Honduras won't extradite Haitian.

text.p: The United States said Wednesday it was "deeply disappointed" that Honduras had refused to extradite a former Haitian police chief and warned the country against becoming a haven for drug traffickers.

Honduras' Supreme Court on Tuesday rejected a U.S. request to extradite Michel Francois, chief of police in the Haitian capital Port-au-Prince during the 1991-94 military regime there, on drug trafficking charges.
It said Washington had failed to supply enough evidence.

"The United States Government is deeply disappointed with the decision made yesterday," said State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns. "We continue to believe that under the terms of the extradition treaty Francois should be extradited to the United States."
Burns said Washington strongly urged the government of the Central American country to take steps that would allow Francois to be brought to trial in the United States.
"If Francois is allowed to enjoy impunity, it will be a signal that the Honduran government is ready to serve as a haven for drug criminals," he added.
Francois arrived in Honduras from the Dominican Republic in April 1996 and was arrested by Honduran police backed by U.S. agents.
Francois said Wednesday he believed the United States would try to kill him now that Honduras has refused to extradite him.
A spokeman for the U.S. Embassy in Honduras said Francois' remarks were groundless.
